walkthrough: Goal: blend paint that is already on the canvas: pull one colour into the next with the pen, soften the edge between two blocks, smudge only inside a selection, move colour inside painted areas without spreading onto the paper, take it back, and find it exactly so after reopening.

Entry: the right island holds, left to right, Brush, Smudge (a fingertip over the trail it smeared, between Brush and Eraser as in Procreate), Eraser, Layers and the colour. On a canvas with a black band above a coloured one, tap Smudge: it takes the ink ring and Brush loses it. Tap it again: the panel headed Smudge lists the same brushes, Soft Brush chosen (the smudge has its own brush, size, strength and StreamLine, each brush its own per tool); tap Smudge once more to close it. The side bar's sliders now read Smudge size and Strength under the hovering pen; Strength starts at 70 %.

Smudge: draw down from the black band through the coloured one and onto the paper. Under the tip the paint is picked up and dragged along: black runs into the colour, the colour runs out onto the paper and thins as it goes; dragging from the empty paper into a band pulls transparency in, so the band fades there. Pressing harder carries more. While the pen is down the brush's outline shows at its tip (it lays no colour of its own to show where it is). Nothing outside the brush's path changes, and the stroke ends where the line got to (no StreamLine catch-up).
Undo: the smudge is gone and the bands are exactly as before; redo: the same smudge again, pixel for pixel.

Selection: tap Selection, Rectangle, and drag a rectangle over the right part of both bands; tap Smudge (the bar goes, the selection stays) and smudge across the selection's left edge from outside: only the inside changes, and the colour from outside is carried in. Tap Selection, then Deselect.

Alpha Lock: open Layers, turn Alpha Lock on, close Layers, and smudge from the coloured band up through the black one onto the paper: colour moves inside the painted bands, and the paper stays white where nothing was painted.
Reopen after the system closed the app: every smudge looks exactly as it did; Smudge is still the tool, with its brush and strength.

Failure and cancel: a locked layer refuses the smudge like any stroke; on an empty layer it moves nothing visible; a cancelled pen contact leaves no trace. Not here: smudging across layers (it only drags the current layer), wet colour mixing, finger smudging, smudge-only brush settings.
